validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: real, well-documented project. Enable Gas Transmission, LLC (EGT) filed FERC Docket No. CP20-482-000 on June 17, 2020 (Federal Register notice, 2020-07-06, verified) for the 'MASS project' (Enable's own name for it, per its 10-K glossary). Enable Midstream Partners' SEC 8-K (2021-05-03) confirms 'Enable Gas Transmission, LLC's MASS project was placed into service April 1, 2021,' backed by a 5-year firm precedent agreement. EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook (Historical Projects tab, row 'MASS Project', operator 'Enable Gas Transmission', Docket CP20-482) independently tracks the same project as Completed. Correctly classified as gas transmission (natural gas takeaway from the Anadarko/Arkoma basins) -- not a duplicate of any other roster row (no other PID references CP20-482 or 'MASS'). However, five recorded data points on this row disagree with these same primary sources -- see the following concern records; none of them touch existence or classification.

validity.recommendation: Correct LengthKnown from 0 to 1.5 (LengthKnownUnits=mi, ~2.4 km) -- this is not a compression-only, zero-new-pipe expansion.
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet records LengthKnown=0.00 km, consistent with the batch brief's general rule for the five len=0 Enable/NGPL/PNGTS rows ('expansion with no new physical pipe'). That rule does NOT hold for this row. The Federal Register notice of FERC Docket CP20-482 (verified, primary regulatory document) states the project scope explicitly begins with item (i): 'install a NEW 1.5-MILE PIPELINE that will provide transportation service from EGT's existing Delhi Compressor Station to a tap on EGT's existing Line CP' -- i.e. new physical pipe, not just compressor/auxiliary work. EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook independently lists 'Miles = 1.5' for this same project (Docket CP20-482), corroborating the FERC filing from a second, independent government-data origin. Two independent primary sources agree on 1.5 miles of new pipe; recommend LengthKnown=1.5, LengthKnownUnits=mi (2.41 km) rather than 0.

validity.recommendation: Correct ConstructionYear from 2021 to 2020, and StartYear1 from 2022 to 2021 (April).
validity.researcher_notes: Enable Midstream Partners' FY2020 10-K (SEC, verified) states: 'we invested $49 million of expansion capital in the construction of transportation pipeline and facilities, including ... construction of the MASS project, which began during 2020' -- construction start is 2020, not the recorded 2021, and Enable's own Q3-2020 8-K (verified, filed 2020-11-04) independently describes construction as having 'recently began' as of that filing, consistent with a 2020 start. Enable's Q1-2021 8-K earnings release (SEC, verified, EX-99.1 dated 2021-05-03) states: 'Enable Gas Transmission, LLC's MASS project was placed into service April 1, 2021' -- in-service is April 2021, not the recorded 2022. EIA's pipeline-projects workbook independently corroborates: Completed Date 2021-04-01, Year In Service Date 2021. Two independent origins (Enable/SEC + EIA) agree the project was in service April 2021, a full year before the sheet's StartYear1=2022; the construction-start year rests on Enable's own filings only (single publisher, two dated documents).

validity.recommendation: Location is likely incomplete/wrong as OK->OK; the project's own FERC filing places facilities in Arkansas, Louisiana AND Oklahoma. Recommend reviewing whether EndState/Province should read Louisiana (candidate) rather than Oklahoma, or that the row's location be documented as a multi-state/multi-site project.
validity.researcher_notes: Sheet records StartState/Province=Oklahoma and EndState/Province=Oklahoma (both). The Federal Register notice of FERC Docket CP20-482 (verified, primary) states: 'All project work will be conducted within Clark and Jackson Counties, Arkansas; Richland Parish, Louisiana; and Grady and McClain Counties, Oklahoma.' This is a single project with six facility items spread across three states, NOT an Oklahoma-only footprint -- EIA's own state tag (Beg_State=End_State=OK, 'Crosses State Border'=No) is an oversimplification that the sheet appears to have copied. The new 1.5-mile pipe (item i) runs 'from EGT's existing Delhi Compressor Station to a tap on EGT's existing Line CP'; Richland Parish, LA contains the town of Delhi and the Perryville Hub area, where EGT and several other interstate systems interconnect, which is consistent with (but does not conclusively prove) the new pipe segment itself sitting in Louisiana while the Anadarko-basin-facing compressor upgrades (Amber Junction CS, Grady/McClain counties) anchor the Oklahoma end -- this Start=OK/End=LA read is my inference from the supply(OK)->Gulf-Coast-delivery(LA) narrative in Enable's own SEC filings, not something the FERC notice states in so many words. What IS certain and directly sourced: Oklahoma-only is wrong; Arkansas and Louisiana are also physically part of this project. Only one truly independent primary source (the FERC/Federal Register notice) states the county list, and it conflicts with EIA's simpler state tag -- flagging for human review rather than confidently overwriting a specific Start/End pair.

validity.recommendation: Add Arkoma Basin alongside Anadarko Basin in FuelSource.
validity.researcher_notes: Sheet records FuelSource='Anadarko Basin' only. Enable's own FY2020 10-K glossary defines the MASS project as: 'A supply driven project designed to deliver gas from the Anadarko and Arkoma Basins to delivery points with access to emerging Gulf Coast markets and growing demand markets in the Southeast.' The Q1-2021 8-K repeats the identical framing: 'transports natural gas from the Anadarko and Arkoma Basins.' Both are Enable/SEC filings (one origin). EIA's project notes say only 'Takeaway capacity out of Anadarko basin' -- a second, independent origin, but one that is silent on Arkoma rather than contradicting it. Net: Anadarko is doubly confirmed; Arkoma rests on Enable's own (repeated, but single-origin) disclosure -- tier medium rather than high on the Arkoma addition specifically.

validity.recommendation: Re-check the basis for Delayed=yes/DelayType=confirmed; independent evidence found points the other way (on-time or early completion).
validity.researcher_notes: Sheet records Delayed=yes, DelayType=confirmed, with no ref. I could not find any source describing a delay on this project. To the contrary, FOUR consecutive Enable/SEC quarterly disclosures show unbroken on-schedule guidance: Q3-2019 (precedent agreement signed Oct 2019 following a successful open season) -> Q2-2020 8-K ('remains on schedule and is expected to be placed into service in the second quarter of 2021') -> Q3-2020 8-K (construction 'recently began following the receipt of all regulatory approvals,' no schedule change noted) -> Q4-2020 8-K ('Construction continues ... still anticipated to be placed into service during the second quarter of 2021') -> Q1-2021 8-K (placed into service April 1, 2021 -- i.e. within, not behind, the Q2-2021 guidance repeated across three prior quarters). This is a stronger negative case than a single missing-delay-mention: it is affirmative, repeated, contemporaneous on-schedule language across 18 months of filings, with the actual completion landing on or ahead of every guidance date given. All four documents are Enable/SEC filings (one publisher), and none of them (nor the FERC docket, nor EIA) states what originally justified the sheet's 'confirmed' delay flag, so I have not overridden the value outright -- flagging here for a reviewer to weigh against whatever originally justified it.
